The graph advanced design-review to 'ready' (frontier_auto_advance) and fired it twice without the audit findings it was designed to weigh, so any claimed completion would be baseless and would poison the milestone/audit nodes that depend on this decision record.

The node's why is explicit: it is the judgment step that weighs audit findings and resolves the Phase-2 node set from assessed state, protecting the invariant that implementation direction follows from assessment. Its sole required artifact is audits/design-review.md. Direct inspection of the eval worktree (a git worktree of /Users/sab-mini/repos/aa-cli) shows: (a) no audits/ directory exists; (b) no design-review.md or tui-methodology.md anywhere on disk; (c) the diff between the two attempt commits is empty — the executor produced zero repo changes across both attempts; (d) the upstream tui-methodology-audit node is still 'provisional' in the config graph with its artifact missing, meaning the review ran with no findings to judge; (e) the harness scratch files indicate the run was actually working on a different node (common-core from the pilot graph). Every acceptance criterion is indeterminate with no supporting evidence, and the required artifact is flagged absent. Intent is not preserved (nothing was delivered toward the judgment role), and graph integrity is not preserved (the graph recorded two execution attempts and advanced the frontier for a review whose decision record — the basis for Phase-2 authorizations and downstream milestone/audit nodes — does not exist; dependents firing on this state would build on nothing). This warrants a block with human review before the frontier advances further; lane 1's criteria verdict is not re-adjudicated here, but the absence of any artifact makes the node's role objectively unfulfilled.
